# September account update

The September update is available to hosted accounts. This release changes how account credits appear, adds a billing export, and improves the member search. Administrators will see the new controls when they next open Settings.

## Credits on invoices

A credit is now shown against the invoice it reduces, rather than as an adjustment to the amount displayed on the account page. The invoice lists its original total, the credit applied, and the remaining amount to pay. A credit larger than the invoice leaves a balance available for a later invoice.

Previously downloaded invoices keep their original layout. You can obtain the new layout by downloading the invoice again. The invoice number stays the same, which allows finance teams to replace their saved PDF without changing the reference in their ledger.

## Exporting billing records

The export covers the date range selected in Billing and includes one row per invoice. Amounts are provided in the invoice currency. If your account has invoices in more than one currency, group the rows by currency before adding the amounts.

Choose whether to include voided invoices before starting the download. Their rows carry a void status and the date of the void. We include them so that teams reconciling an invoice sequence can account for a number that otherwise appears to be missing.

- The invoice date determines whether a row falls inside the selected period.
- The paid date is a separate column and can fall outside that period.
- The download includes the account name saved on each invoice.

The export uses the permissions of the person requesting it. An administrator who manages two accounts must download each account separately. A report started before this update will finish in its original format; start another export to obtain the additional columns.

## Finding members

Member search now accepts an email domain as well as a person's name. Searching for a domain returns both active and suspended members. Use the status filter to narrow the results before selecting people for a bulk action.

The search field keeps your last query while you move between result pages. Returning from a member's details also restores the page you were viewing. This should make it easier to work through a long result list without repeatedly navigating from the beginning.

## PDF and email changes

Invoice PDFs now place the purchase-order reference above the item list. When a credit is used, the original invoice total remains visible alongside the amount deducted and the amount still due; any unused credit remains available for a subsequent invoice. The footer also includes the billing contact's email address, and long company names can run onto a second line without covering the postal code.

Invoice emails use the contact name saved in Billing. Changing that name affects future messages; it leaves messages already sent in your mail archive unchanged. The payment link continues to open the invoice in the browser.

## Availability

Self-hosted administrators can install the update during their normal maintenance window. Back up the configuration before replacing the application files. The release package includes a migration check that reports any required account-field changes before installation proceeds.

Contact support with the account reference and export date if a download fails. Those details let us find the request without asking you to attach financial records.

# Choosing the freezer for the annex

## Capacity

The smaller model holds the weekly delivery with two baskets spare. We measured the cartons rather than relying on the advertised capacity, because the large soup tubs have to stand upright. The larger model would take another delivery, but our supplier comes twice a week and the kitchen has no plan to increase its order.

The smaller freezer is sufficient for the annex.

## Access and installation

Both models fit through the external kitchen door. The larger model needs the door removed from its hinges; the installer has included that work in the quote. The smaller one can be wheeled straight in. Either installation needs the old freezer emptied by eight on the delivery morning.

Facilities has checked the sockets and allocated a circuit. The supplier will take the old appliance away if it is disconnected and ready beside the loading door. The porter has offered to clear that space after the breakfast delivery.

The smaller model has enough capacity for the annex.

## Purchase

The kitchen manager has already approved the smaller model on the capacity test. Purchasing now needs the asset code and delivery date to complete the order. I have requested the code from finance and asked the supplier to hold Tuesday's slot until tomorrow afternoon. The temporary hire ends on Wednesday, so that slot avoids another week's hire charge.

# Saturday repair workshop: room setup and clear-down

The hall will be shared with the afternoon class. Our booking runs from nine until one, including setup and packing. Leave the centre aisle open throughout: it is the route from the entrance to the rear exit, and visitors will be carrying objects that can obscure their view of the floor.

## Opening the room

Collect the key from reception and check the room before bringing in equipment. If furniture has been left in the aisle, move it to the marked storage area first. The room diagram is fixed beside the light switches, with the table positions marked in blue.

Two volunteers should unfold the long tables while the others bring in the repair boxes. Check that each table's legs have locked before placing tools on it. Put the job-registration desk beside the entrance, far enough inside for someone to open the door while another visitor completes a ticket.

The registration volunteer should write a ticket for every object and give the owner the matching numbered slip. Photograph any existing damage with the owner's agreement. This makes it easier to distinguish the condition on arrival from the work carried out during the session.

## During the session

Keep loose parts in a tray bearing the job number. Use a separate tray for each object, even when the same volunteer is working on both. Replacement parts purchased from the workshop stock should be recorded on the ticket so the treasurer can replenish the right items.

The tea station belongs against the window wall. Place the collection tin behind the cups and keep the registration desk free for new arrivals. Visitors waiting for a repair can sit in the front row of chairs, where they can hear their number called without standing beside a workbench.

At eleven thirty, the registration volunteer should check the waiting jobs with the repair team before accepting anything else. A repair already under way can continue until twelve fifteen. Explain the collection arrangements to owners whose jobs need a part we do not have; include the part description and the volunteer's contact address on their ticket.

## Packing and moving equipment

At twelve fifteen, stop taking work to the benches. Ask owners to collect completed jobs before folding tables. Put unfinished jobs into their labelled boxes with the tickets inside, then count tools against the inventory kept in the lid of each tool case.

The trolley now has to cross the room several times as packed boxes go to the store. Keep the centre aisle clear during those journeys, including while completed repairs are waiting for collection. Put those repairs on the side bench rather than in the trolley's path.

- Check under every table for screws and small parts.
- Wipe the work surfaces before folding them.
- Return chairs to the positions shown on the room diagram.
- Record missing tools on the inventory sheet.

## Handover

The last two volunteers should walk through the room together after the equipment has gone. Check the storage door, windows, and tea station. Take the key and completed attendance sheet to reception, where the afternoon tutor will collect the key. Leave the signed inventory in the workshop cupboard for next week's team.

# First week with the new reading room

We opened the upstairs reading room on Monday. The downstairs room now closes at four because the evening language classes need its tables. We moved the local-history books upstairs so people consulting them could continue until the building closes at seven.

There were more boxes than the lift could hold in one trip. On Sunday, two volunteers numbered them in shelf order and put the numbers on a floor plan. That let us carry up the boxes while the shelving team worked through the room from the window wall towards the door. The maps went in the flat drawers nearest the desk.

The signs were the slow part. We had printed the old room number on the membership forms, and there were still two arrows on the ground floor pointing towards the classroom. I covered those with temporary cards while Lina changed the master file. We used large print on the cards because visitors tend to look for directions while they are still walking.

On Tuesday, a researcher arrived with a list of street directories spanning twenty years. We found three upstairs and ordered the remaining volumes from the store. She booked the same desk for Thursday, when the delivery van would bring the requested books. The desk numbers are now on the booking sheet, which lets staff put requested material in the right place before a visit.

At the upstairs desk, we keep pencils, request slips, and a folder of photocopy orders. Moving the local-history collection upstairs means it remains available until seven, after the downstairs room is taken over for classes at four. The folder has separate pockets for orders awaiting payment and orders ready to collect; Lina reconciles those against the till receipt before she leaves.

Thursday was the first evening with every desk occupied. One reader asked for a stronger lamp, so we exchanged the lamp on desk six with the adjustable one from the office. Another wanted to spread out a folded map. Staff cleared the end desk for her and moved its reservation card to the neighbouring place.

On Friday I counted the unused request slips and ordered another pad. Lina sent the corrected membership form to the printer. We left the temporary direction cards in place for the weekend, since the permanent signs were still waiting for their fixing strips.

The labels on our new freezer arrived in a flat envelope marked "This way up." I put the envelope on the kitchen table and went to find the delivery note. We had ordered dividers as well as labels, and the invoice listed both, but only one parcel had come through the door.

The supplier found the second parcel at the depot. It would arrive the following morning, too late for the first delivery of soup. I borrowed three shallow crates from the pantry and measured them against the freezer baskets. Two fitted side by side. The third had handles that caught against the rim, so we left it for the bread.

By lunch, every tub had a date label and the stock sheet showed which basket held each batch. Nora copied the basket numbers onto the delivery clipboard. The empty label envelope stayed on the table under a mug while we cleaned the shelves.

At four, the courier returned. He had found the dividers behind another delivery in his van and brought them before finishing his route. We thanked him and shifted the tubs into the divided baskets while the kitchen was between services.

Nora picked up the empty envelope to put it in the paper bin. "This way up," she read, then turned the clipboard round so I could sign the stock sheet. I had been trying to read it upside down. She carried the signed sheet to the freezer door and clipped it beneath the basket plan.

# Export notes for the attendance register

Choose one row per visit when you need to count sessions attended. A person who came on three dates appears on three rows. The same person is listed again for each visit.

## Names and totals

The name column contains the spelling saved on the membership record. The date column contains the date of the visit. The fee column contains the amount charged for that visit.

Use the membership number when grouping rows: two people can share a name, and one person may have changed their surname during the year. Keep cancelled visits in a separate group if you are reconciling refunds.

## Saving the file

The download is called attendance.csv. Save it in the folder for the reporting month before opening it in the spreadsheet application. That keeps the downloaded version available if you need to check a formula later.

Choose one row per person for the mailing list. In that export, a member appears once and the file includes the current contact address. Members who have opted out of email still appear, with their preference in a separate column. Filter on that column before passing addresses to the mailing service.

Both exports include the date they were generated in the final column.

# Courtyard booking trial: first-month review

The trial should continue with the current booking sheet. It lets the caretaker resolve overlapping requests before residents send invitations, and all three overlaps this month were settled that way. Replacing it with an open online calendar would remove that confirmation step unless we also built an approval process.

## What residents booked

There were fourteen gatherings in May. Ten used the folding tables and chairs, and four brought their own furniture. Most bookings were on Saturday afternoons. Two households cancelled because of rain; both told the caretaker early enough for the furniture collection to be cancelled as well.

The busiest afternoon had three consecutive bookings. The middle group returned the tables late, leaving the last host to collect them from the courtyard rather than the store. The caretaker has added a space for the agreed return time beside the furniture request. That gives him a time to check against when another collection follows.

## Access

The side gate worked well for most gatherings. One host could not hear the bell from the far end of the courtyard and asked a guest to wait near the gate. Maintenance has checked the bell and will move the receiver nearer the external door. The wiring can stay where it is, so this work fits within the maintenance allowance already agreed.

We received one report that guests had propped open the main entrance. The host was contacted that evening and closed it. The existing gate instructions remain on the confirmation slip; the caretaker will hand that slip over with the furniture key.

## Records

Hello Mara,

Your replacement kettle is covered by the original purchase warranty. A replacement carries the remaining time on that warranty rather than starting another two-year period, so the cover ends on 18 February. The dispatch confirmation uses the replacement's serial number, which is why it looks like a new purchase in your account.

I have attached the inspection team's return label. Please empty the kettle and let it dry before packing it. The outer box can be any suitable cardboard box; we do not require the retail packaging. Put the fault reference inside so the inspection team can match the parcel to this conversation.

You asked whether to include the base. Please send it with the kettle because the team needs to test the connection between them. Keep the spare filter you bought separately. It fits the replacement and is not part of the fault assessment.

The inspection team will check the shut-off switch as well as the connection you reported. If they reproduce the fault, they will add the finding to the replacement record; you do not need to open a separate claim. The replacement will arrive with a new base, so please avoid keeping the old base as a spare when packing this return.

The collection can take place on Tuesday or Thursday. Reply with your preferred day and the address where somebody can hand over the parcel. Collections run throughout the day, and the driver cannot call ahead. I can arrange delivery to your workplace if receiving the replacement at home is difficult.

The replacement's warranty therefore runs only until 18 February: it takes over the unused portion of your original cover rather than beginning a fresh two years. I will send the collection confirmation once you choose a day.

Regards,
Leah

The two entries you see are a pending card authorization and the completed payment for your bicycle hire. We have taken one payment of 42 pounds. The pending entry reserves funds while the bank processes the transaction; your bank controls when that reservation disappears.

I checked the return record as well. Your bicycle was scanned back into the station at 17:46, within the booked period, and the receipt attached here shows the full hire charge. There is no additional late-return charge on this booking. The station screen briefly lost its connection yesterday, so the confirmation email was sent after the physical return.

For your expense claim, use the attached receipt rather than a screenshot of the banking app. The receipt includes the hire date, business address, and tax breakdown. If your employer needs its company name on the receipt, reply with that name and I can reissue the document under the same receipt number.

If the pending authorization becomes a second completed payment, send us the dates and the last four digits of the card through this ticket. That would be a different state from the temporary reservation visible today, and we would ask our payments team to trace both settlement references. Please leave the middle card digits out of your message.

You can keep using your hire account while the bank releases the reservation. Your next booking will have its own receipt and will appear separately in the booking history.

Hello Nina,

I have restored access to your photography course. The lessons open under the email address used for the gift redemption, which is your personal address. Your work address has the purchase receipt but does not have an enrolled student profile.

Please reply if either device opens a purchase page instead of the lessons. Tell me which device it was and the email shown under Account; a screenshot of the lesson list is enough, without forwarding the sign-in code.

Regards,
Amina

I recommend keeping the original train booking and changing the passenger name. The operator allows a name correction on this fare for 8 pounds, while cancelling would forfeit the fare. Our amendment team can make the correction once you confirm the spelling shown on your identification.

Your seat reservation is in coach C, seat 34. The amendment keeps that reservation, including the table position you requested. You will receive a replacement ticket by email, and the old barcode will stop working when the amendment is issued. Please remove the old ticket from your phone wallet afterwards.

The bicycle reservation is recorded separately. It is under the same surname and will be updated by the amendment team during the same request. You will get a second attachment for the bicycle, which the train staff may ask to see before loading.

Keeping the booking and correcting the name remains the best route because the 8-pound correction avoids losing the fare through cancellation. Please send the correct full name by replying to this ticket before 16:00 tomorrow. That leaves the team time to issue both attachments before you travel.

Thank you,
Ruth

Our amendment team can make the correction once you confirm the spelling shown on your identification.

Your seat reservation is in coach C, seat 34. The amendment keeps that reservation, including the table position you requested. Keeping the booking and correcting the name remains the best route because the 8-pound correction avoids losing the fare through cancellation. Please send the correct full name by replying to this ticket before 16:00 tomorrow. That leaves the team time to issue both attachments before you travel.

Thank you,
Ruth

Hello Alex,

Your wallpaper order can be returned. The return period ends on 9 June. That is the final date for starting the return request. You have already contacted us within that period, so I have opened return R618 for the four unopened rolls.

The opened sample roll is yours to keep. We sell samples separately and do not ask customers to return them with unused stock. The four full rolls should retain their batch labels, because the warehouse checks those labels against the original order before issuing the refund. A photograph of the rolls together is enough for the preliminary check.

You can choose collection or post the rolls yourself. Collection costs 12 pounds, deducted from the refund, and takes place on weekdays. If you post them, put R618 on a note inside the parcel and keep the tracking receipt until we confirm arrival. The postal address is on the return slip attached to this message.

The refund goes back to the card used for the order. Your recent address change affects the collection address but does not change the payment destination. Please confirm whether the collection should be from your new flat or the original delivery address.

For collection, reply with the address and a weekday when someone will be there. For self-posting, print the attached return slip, include R618 inside, and retain the tracking receipt. Either route uses the same return record, so please choose one before sending the rolls.

Regards,
Kai

Hi Beth,

The captions are available with your recording, but they are stored as a separate file. Your video player reads that file alongside the video, which is why moving only the video to the shared drive removed the captions from playback.

Open the recording page and choose Download captions. Save the file in the same shared folder as the video. I have enabled downloads for your account again until Monday so you can retrieve it without asking the meeting owner to change the recording's permissions.

The attendee list is in Reports rather than on the recording page. It lists everyone who joined, including people who left before the recording began. If you need a list restricted to the recorded session, use the join and leave times to make that selection before sharing it.

The missing words on screen result from the caption file being separate from the movie; copying the movie alone leaves the player without the accompanying text. Your meeting title can also be changed on the recording page, and the new title will appear on future downloads.

There is no need to upload the video again. Reply once you have saved the captions if the player still fails to show them, and tell me which player you are using.

Best,
Sanjay

Hello Jo,

Your garden membership is active. The gate reader uses a stored list that updates overnight, so a membership renewed this afternoon will work at the gate tomorrow morning. I have sent a temporary entry code for today's visit in a separate message.

The potting shed key can be collected from the office until 17:00. Please bring the numbered tag from your old keyring; we exchange that tag when issuing a key. If you have lost it, the office can look up the number using your plot reference.

For gate access, today's renewal reaches the reader during the overnight update, which is why the card will begin opening the gate tomorrow. The office is beside the north entrance, opposite the water tanks.

Your compost delivery is also confirmed for Saturday. The driver will leave the bags at the communal unloading bay, where plot holders can use the garden trolley. Delivery times are assigned on Friday, and we will text the window to the mobile number ending 61.

The card's delay is simply the reader waiting for tonight's membership-list refresh; after that refresh your renewed membership will be recognized tomorrow morning. Let me know if the temporary code has not arrived, and I can check the destination number.

Regards,
Mo

documents.text:
Hello Daniel,

The smoke alarm you ordered takes a sealed battery, and we have booked a replacement for the unit that keeps chirping. Please leave the working alarms installed while you wait. The return label applies only to the faulty unit whose serial number ends 284.

The replacement is due on Wednesday. It comes with its own mounting plate, screws, and instruction leaflet. The plate is different from your older model's plate, so the installer will need to change it. We can arrange an installer appointment after you confirm that the parcel has arrived. Please keep the delivery note for that appointment.

Our returns team needs a short description of the chirping interval. You have already supplied the recording, and I have attached it to the case, so you do not need to send another one. The serial number photograph is also legible.

When packing the faulty alarm after the installer removes it, keep the working alarms in place. Taking down the whole set to compare serial numbers would leave the other rooms uncovered while the return travels. The installer can check the labels on those units without leaving them off the ceilings. Put only unit 284 in the return box.

Reply with the delivery confirmation when the replacement arrives and give us two suitable appointment dates. The installer can take the faulty alarm away, or you can use the return label if you prefer to post it later.

Regards,
Ellen

Hi Tess,

The extra space at the centre of your photo-book spread is the printer's binding allowance. Images that cross the centre need that allowance so the fold does not hide part of the picture; it is included automatically and does not add to the price.

I have checked your proof and found two photographs below the recommended resolution. They are on pages 12 and 19. Hello Iona,

I suggest repairing the clasp rather than replacing the whole necklace, provided the jeweller confirms the chain itself is sound. The photograph shows a bent clasp spring, and a clasp repair is included in the service cover. A replacement necklace would use your one replacement allowance.

There are two practical routes. A postal repair is free and usually takes ten working days from arrival. We send a padded box and an insured label. You would need to keep the necklace until the box arrives rather than posting it in a paper envelope. The repair team returns it to the address on the service record.

Alternatively, our partner shop can inspect it on Saturday. The inspection is free, but any same-day repair depends on whether the right clasp is in stock. The shop can order a clasp if needed, and you can collect the necklace later instead of arranging another delivery. You mentioned that you work nearby on Wednesdays, so that might suit you.

A full replacement becomes the sensible option if the inspection finds stretched chain links as well as the clasp fault. That would replace both damaged parts, but your replacement allowance would then be used. The shop will ask for approval before making that change.

Given the clasp-only fault visible so far and your Wednesday visits nearby, book the Saturday inspection and plan to collect a repaired necklace on Wednesday. If the chain is also damaged, ask the shop to price the replacement route before using your allowance. I can make the inspection booking once you confirm a time.

Regards,
Hal

Hi Rob,

I have found your language-test result. The certificate is issued under the name on the identity document checked on test day, so it currently shows Robert rather than Rob. We can change the correspondence name on your account without changing that certificate.

Your university has asked for direct verification. Give its admissions office the result reference shown at the top of the certificate. An authorized officer can use that reference with your date of birth to verify the score. I have enabled verification for the university you named and sent you a confirmation of that access.

You can download a replacement copy of the certificate under Results. It will show the same identity-document name and score, with today's download date in the footer. That date records when the copy was produced; the test date remains in the main certificate heading.

Changing the account's correspondence name to Rob will affect future reminders and booking emails immediately. Changing the certificate to Rob would require identity evidence supporting that name, which our certificates team would examine separately. If you want that examination, attach the evidence through the secure document area rather than replying by email.

For the university deadline on Monday, the existing certificate and the direct verification reference are ready to use now. The admissions office can verify the result while a name-change request is being considered. Please tell me if it encounters an access error and include the wording of the error message.

Best,
Frances

Hello Priya,

The address on your parcel cannot be changed now because it has already entered the carrier's network. Please use the carrier's delivery manager to request collection from a local depot instead. The link in yesterday's dispatch email opens the correct parcel record.

Your second order is still in our warehouse. I have changed that delivery address to the office address you supplied and asked the packing team to check the label before dispatch. That order contains the replacement lampshade, packed separately from the first parcel's lamp base.

The shade's carton includes the small fitting ring. Please keep it when unpacking, since it sits beneath the bulb holder and can easily be mistaken for packing material. The fitting diagram is inside the carton lid.

For the first parcel, depot collection through the carrier remains the recommended route: the parcel is already in their network, so we can no longer amend its delivery address. The carrier's opening hours will appear when you select a depot.

The office delivery label will include your department name. Our carrier normally hands workplace parcels to reception rather than taking them to an individual desk, so please ask reception to keep the carton upright until you collect it. If the carton shows damage, a photograph taken before opening will help us match any broken shade to the delivery condition. I have added your office extension to the warehouse notes, where the packing team can see it if they need to confirm the label.

The lampshade order will go to your office. I will send its new tracking number once the warehouse hands it over, and you can reply to that message if the label preview shows anything unexpected.

Regards,
Ben

Hi Martin,

The reading lamp dims through its base switch. Keep a finger on the switch to change the brightness; a quick touch only turns the light on or off. The lamp remembers the last brightness when you switch it off at the base.

The wall timer interrupts power rather than sending a command to that switch. After a power interruption the lamp starts in standby, which explains why the timer can turn it off but cannot make it come on again. That behavior is different from the brightness memory used when the lamp remains connected to power.

I checked the extension lead in your photograph. It has enough space around the plug adapter, and its switch is accessible. You can leave the lamp powered there and operate it at the base. If reaching the base is difficult, we can exchange it for the model with a wired hand control; the exchange window is open until the end of this month.

The dimming instruction above should let you test whether the current lamp is comfortable at the desk. Try the lower brightness with your usual reading material rather than checking the light against a blank tabletop. If glare remains a problem, the exchange model also has a wider shade.

Tell me whether the base control is convenient after that test. I can then either close this ticket or arrange the exchange and collection together.

Regards,
Ada

Hello Sal,

To prepare for your visit:

Chris

Hi Amelia,

Your cloud backup has finished, but the album order on the new phone is still being built. Photos arrive before the album index, so the pictures can be visible while their albums remain empty. Leave the app connected to Wi-Fi and power tonight so it can finish arranging them.

I found the three videos you mentioned in the backup record. They were uploaded as original files, and the new phone will download viewing copies first. The empty albums are a result of the index arriving after the photos; the images have reached the phone before their album membership has been applied. Your shared family album has a separate invitation, which I have re-sent to your current address.

You can continue taking photographs during this process. They will join the next backup when the phone connects. If the album count is unchanged tomorrow morning, reply with a screenshot of the sync status at the bottom of the Library screen. Please keep the app installed so the support record retains its current sync identifier.

Regards,
George

Dispatch 4.2 is now available. This update covers route planning, driver notes, and the daily vehicle list. Existing routes keep their assigned drivers when the update is installed.

A route's departure time is now stored in the depot's local time zone. When a planner in another time zone opens that route, the departure time stays tied to the depot instead of shifting to the planner's local time. The depot name appears beside the time field. Routes copied to another depot use the destination depot's zone, and the copy screen shows that zone before confirmation.

Driver notes can include photographs. Drivers can attach up to four images to a stop, and dispatchers can open them from the stop history. Images remain with that history after a route is archived. Downloaded route sheets include a photograph count rather than the images themselves, keeping the sheets small enough to print in the cab.

The vehicle list has a new Out of service filter and a column for the next inspection date. Vehicles marked out of service remain visible on past routes, where their registration is part of the delivery record. The list also keeps your column widths between visits. A route continues to show its departure in the depot's time zone even when the person viewing it works elsewhere, rather than converting it to that person's local time.

We fixed a problem that could leave a duplicate stop after a failed drag operation. We also corrected the print layout for addresses longer than three lines. Hosted depots receive the update tonight; managed installations can download the package from their administration page. The installation check requires every active depot to have a time zone selected and lists the depots that need attention before it proceeds.

# Studio 6.1

The new release adds recoverable deletions for projects and makes shared folders easier to audit. It is available today for browser users; desktop users will see an update notice on their next launch.

## Deleted projects

Deleted projects go into the workspace bin for thirty days. During that period an owner can restore a project with its folders and comments. Files already downloaded by a collaborator remain on that person's device. The bin shows the deletion date and the person who deleted the project.

Workspace owners can empty the bin early. Emptying it permanently removes the selected projects, and the confirmation screen lists their names before the action is accepted. Collaborators cannot empty the bin, even when they originally created a project.

## Shared-folder audit

The access panel now shows whether a person has direct access to a folder or inherits it through a project role. Removing a direct invitation leaves inherited access in place. To remove inherited access, change the person's role on the parent project.

An export of the access panel includes the source of each permission. The file records access at the moment the export starts; changes made during a long download appear in the next export. Dates are supplied in the workspace's time zone.

## Recovering work

For a project deleted by mistake, open Workspace settings, choose Bin, select the project, and choose Restore. Its previous members regain their roles, so check the access panel before adding new files. This is the recovery route during the thirty-day period described above. Once a project has been permanently removed, the bin will show its removal record without a Restore button.

## Before emptying the bin

The bin may contain projects other people still expect to recover. Read the selected names and deletion dates before confirming permanent removal, especially when using Select all. The confirmation is the last stage at which you can cancel. Routine updates leave the bin contents and their original thirty-day deadlines unchanged.

paragraphs.text: The new release adds recoverable deletions for projects and makes shared folders easier to audit. It is available today for browser users; desktop users will see an update notice on their next launch.

Deleted projects go into the workspace bin for thirty days. During that period an owner can restore a project with its folders and comments. Files already downloaded by a collaborator remain on that person's device. The bin shows the deletion date and the person who deleted the project.

Workspace owners can empty the bin early. Emptying it permanently removes the selected projects, and the confirmation screen lists their names before the action is accepted. Collaborators cannot empty the bin, even when they originally created a project.

The access panel now shows whether a person has direct access to a folder or inherits it through a project role. Removing a direct invitation leaves inherited access in place. To remove inherited access, change the person's role on the parent project.

An export of the access panel includes the source of each permission. The file records access at the moment the export starts; changes made during a long download appear in the next export. Dates are supplied in the workspace's time zone.

For a project deleted by mistake, open Workspace settings, choose Bin, select the project, and choose Restore. Its previous members regain their roles, so check the access panel before adding new files. This is the recovery route during the thirty-day period described above. Once a project has been permanently removed, the bin will show its removal record without a Restore button.

The bin may contain projects other people still expect to recover. Read the selected names and deletion dates before confirming permanent removal, especially when using Select all. The confirmation is the last stage at which you can cancel. Routine updates leave the bin contents and their original thirty-day deadlines unchanged.

# Catalogue update: alternative item codes

The July catalogue release is ready for all branches. It adds alternative item codes, improves stocktake printing, and corrects two transfer-screen errors. Branch managers can install it after closing their tills.

An item can now have several supplier codes attached to one stock record. Scanning any of those codes opens the same item and changes the same stock balance, so receiving a substitute carton does not create another item. Add codes on the item's Suppliers tab; the original internal code stays unchanged.

Stocktake sheets can be printed by aisle and shelf. The print preview shows the selected location above every page, and empty shelves can be included for checking. Handwritten adjustments still need to be entered through the stocktake screen. A sheet printed before a count begins carries a Draft watermark to distinguish it from an active count. The new code mapping means that different suppliers' barcodes point to one item and one stock balance instead of making separate records for substitute packaging.

Transfers now preserve a note when the receiving branch changes the delivery date. We also fixed a display error that hid fractional quantities on the confirmation page. Quantities in the transfer ledger were correct throughout; this change makes the confirmation page show the same decimal places. Training accounts receive an extra demonstration item with three supplier codes, and managers can remove it from the training catalogue after their practice session.

Before installing, finish or cancel any stocktake that is currently open. The installer checks for active counts and lists them by branch. Alternative codes share the existing item's stock record, with every recognized supplier code updating that single balance. Printed guides and the branch help menu will be updated alongside the release. Please send installation questions with the branch number and the installer message so support can locate the relevant log.

# Rostering 8.0

This release separates shift templates from published shifts. A template is a reusable pattern. Published shifts are dated assignments that staff can see in their calendars. Editing a template affects future uses of that template; it leaves already published shifts unchanged.

## Making a new week

Choose the week, select a template, and review the proposed assignments. Vacant positions appear alongside named staff so a manager can fill them before publishing. The preview marks staff who are unavailable or would exceed their contracted hours. Saving the preview creates a draft week, which staff cannot yet see.

The availability panel now accepts partial-day exceptions. A person who is available until noon can be assigned a morning shift while the afternoon remains blocked. Imported full-day absences keep their current behavior. Managers can add a note to an exception, and the person concerned can read it in their own availability calendar.

## Changing this week's rota

To change a shift staff can already see, open the dated week rather than the template. Select the shift, make the change, and choose Publish changes. The affected staff receive a notification listing the old and new times. Changing the reusable template would leave this week's assignment intact, so this procedure edits the dated shift itself.

## Administration

The activity log now records template changes separately from shift changes. Exports include the editor and timestamp for both, allowing payroll teams to identify when an assignment became visible. Long team names wrap in the week header, and the print view uses the selected week's first day.

For a future pattern change, edit the template and use it when creating the next week. For a correction to a published week, edit its dated shifts and publish the changes. For an absence, enter an availability exception before generating a new draft. These are the three routes managers should choose between when preparing the next rota.

Mailroom 2.7 is available this morning. It adds parcel photographs and changes the way undelivered notices are handled. Scanning and recipient search continue to use the existing desk equipment.

Desk staff can photograph a parcel label after recording its arrival. The photograph appears on the recipient's collection screen and helps distinguish several parcels addressed to the same person. Labels sometimes contain phone numbers, so photographs are visible only to the recipient and authorized mailroom staff. The photograph is removed thirty days after collection, while the collection record remains in the ledger.

Email notices that fail now appear in a Failed notices view. Each entry shows the address used and the delivery error. Staff can correct a mistyped address and resend the notice without creating another parcel record. The second notice keeps the first notice's history. A full mailbox error remains visible until a successful send or manual closure.

For sites where recipients collect by reference number, the printed slip now includes a larger reference and a smaller arrival date. The reference is unchanged by a notice resend. Reprinting a slip records the print time in the activity log, allowing another desk worker to see that a duplicate slip exists. The printer remembers the last selected paper tray for each workstation.

The privacy settings now let a site shorten photograph retention. Choosing seven days removes parcel photographs seven days after collection instead of thirty. It does not shorten the ledger's separate retention period, and changing the setting applies to photographs already waiting for deletion. A confirmation panel shows how many photographs would be removed immediately.

We fixed a scanner-focus problem after closing a recipient search result. Focus now returns to the arrival field, ready for the next parcel. The desk application may briefly reload when the update arrives; scans saved before the reload remain in the ledger.

# Exhibition planner 5.4

Version 5.4 will reach hosted collections on Monday. It includes a floor-plan layer, clearer loan dates, and improved label printing. Local installations can download the same package from the administrator's panel.

## Floor plans

Locked objects now stay in place while you select or move nearby objects. Locking a display case prevents accidental movement without hiding it from the plan. The lock symbol appears in the object list as well as on the canvas. A curator can unlock an individual object from either location.

The plan can also display a scale bar. Choose metres or feet in Plan settings; the selected unit applies to rulers and measurements across the current plan. Existing plans retain the unit they were created with. The exported image includes the scale bar if it is visible when the export begins.

## Loans

Loan records now distinguish the requested return date from the agreed return date. Search and overdue filters use the agreed date once one is entered. Records awaiting a lender's response retain their requested date and show Awaiting agreement beside it. Contact details can be copied directly from the lender panel.

## Printing

Label sheets support a top-margin adjustment for printers that feed paper slightly off centre. The preview includes the selected sheet code, and the test page prints corner marks rather than collection details. Keeping a case locked stops it being shifted inadvertently while surrounding objects are moved, with the case still visible in the drawing. Long artist names now wrap without pushing the accession number onto another label.

## Installation

Back up the collection database before installing the local package. The upgrade checks for unsupported custom label sizes and lists any it finds. You can keep those sizes for existing templates, but new templates must use a supported sheet or a custom single-label size. The release also corrects a keyboard shortcut that could open two search panels after a plan export.

paragraphs.text: Version 5.4 will reach hosted collections on Monday. It includes a floor-plan layer, clearer loan dates, and improved label printing. Local installations can download the same package from the administrator's panel.

Locked objects now stay in place while you select or move nearby objects. Locking a display case prevents accidental movement without hiding it from the plan. The lock symbol appears in the object list as well as on the canvas. A curator can unlock an individual object from either location.

The plan can also display a scale bar. Choose metres or feet in Plan settings; the selected unit applies to rulers and measurements across the current plan. Existing plans retain the unit they were created with. The exported image includes the scale bar if it is visible when the export begins.

Loan records now distinguish the requested return date from the agreed return date. Search and overdue filters use the agreed date once one is entered. Records awaiting a lender's response retain their requested date and show Awaiting agreement beside it. Contact details can be copied directly from the lender panel.

Label sheets support a top-margin adjustment for printers that feed paper slightly off centre. The preview includes the selected sheet code, and the test page prints corner marks rather than collection details. Keeping a case locked stops it being shifted inadvertently while surrounding objects are moved, with the case still visible in the drawing. Long artist names now wrap without pushing the accession number onto another label.

Back up the collection database before installing the local package. The upgrade checks for unsupported custom label sizes and lists any it finds. You can keep those sizes for existing templates, but new templates must use a supported sheet or a custom single-label size. The release also corrects a keyboard shortcut that could open two search panels after a plan export.

# October changes to Field Log

The October update is available for tablets and phones. We recommend downloading it over Wi-Fi before travelling to a survey site. The update leaves downloaded maps on the device.

Draft observations are now saved locally as you type. If the app closes before you submit an observation, reopening it restores the unfinished text on that device. Drafts are not shared with the team until submitted. A small Draft label distinguishes them from observations already waiting to upload.

Map downloads can be named. A name such as North bank survey makes a map easier to identify than its boundary coordinates. The storage screen shows the download date, size, and last time each map was opened. Removing a map leaves its associated observations in the log.

Unfinished entries return when the app is reopened because their text is saved on the device during editing; they remain private drafts until submission. The observation form also has a larger date field and accepts keyboard navigation between coordinate boxes.

Team administrators can export a list of devices that have checked in during the past month. The file includes the device name, app version, and most recent successful upload time. A device can appear there even when it has no observations to send, because opening the team screen performs a check-in.

The coordinate-format preference now appears on printed field sheets. Existing sheets can be downloaded again to add that line without changing their observation numbers. Draft text is kept locally during entry, allowing an interrupted, unsubmitted observation to reopen with its previous wording on the same device.

We corrected a camera rotation error on older tablets and a spacing issue in exported observer names. Please send app-version details with any new report of missing fields; the version is shown at the bottom of Settings.

# Ledger desk 3.3

Credit allocations can now be reversed without deleting the credit itself. This is useful when a credit has been applied to the wrong invoice. The reversal returns the amount to the customer's available credit and records both the allocation and its reversal in the account history.

The allocation screen shows invoice dates, balances, and purchase-order references together. You can sort by any of those columns before choosing an invoice. If two people open the same customer account, the screen checks the available balance again when either person confirms an allocation. The second person sees an updated amount if the first has already used some credit.

Statement PDFs now include page numbers and the account currency in the footer. Customer addresses longer than five lines continue on a second address block instead of covering the statement heading. The download filename includes the statement date, making successive month-end files easier to distinguish.

For finance staff reversing an incorrect allocation, open the customer's history, select the allocation, and choose Reverse. Enter a reason and confirm the amount. Then open Available credit and allocate the returned amount to the correct invoice. This sequence preserves the original credit note and leaves an audit trail of the correction. If the invoice has been included in a closed period, the reversal screen asks for an authorized posting date.

For supervisors checking the correction, search the same history by the credit-note number. The original allocation and its reversal appear as linked entries, followed by any new allocation. Compare their amounts and posting dates before signing off the account. A reviewer can download those entries without receiving permission to change them.

The release also fixes a rounding display on multi-currency statements. Hosted customers receive it tonight, while local administrators can install it after completing their current posting batch. Installation will wait if a batch is still open.

# Booking desk: spring release

Waiting lists are now available for fully booked classes. When a place opens, the first person in the queue receives an offer with a two-hour response window. The place stays reserved for that person during the window. If they decline or the window expires, the next person receives an offer.

Administrators can pause offers for a class while arranging a venue change. People keep their queue positions during the pause. Resuming offers starts a new two-hour window for the next eligible person rather than reviving an expired offer. The activity log records who paused the list and the reason entered.

The room planner now shows the number of portable chairs requested for each class. This count is independent of the room's standard seated capacity, which remains visible below the room name. Printing a setup sheet includes both numbers and the class start time.

The two-hour window uses elapsed time, including overnight hours. A person offered a place at 23:00 would otherwise have to respond by 01:00. To avoid that situation, each venue can set an offer period, such as 08:00 to 20:00. Offers due outside that period wait until the next opening time, and their response window starts when the offer is sent. Already sent offers keep their original deadline.

Before enabling a waiting list, check these settings:

- Confirm the class capacity and whether staff can add exceptional places.
- Set the venue's offer period to match when participants can reasonably respond.
- Choose the contact address used for replies to offers.

We also corrected a calendar print issue affecting classes that cross midnight. Existing fully booked classes will keep their current behavior until an administrator enables their waiting lists.

Survey room 7.2 adds anonymous links, a clearer completion screen, and additional chart labels. The update is available to all workspaces today and applies to surveys created before the release as well as new ones.

Anonymous links now discard the visitor's email address before a response is saved. The resulting response has no email field that an owner can export, even if the visitor arrived from an email campaign. Choose an anonymous link from the Share menu; existing identified campaign links remain identified. The link preview shows which mode you selected.

Completion screens can include a contact button. Survey owners choose its label and destination, and the preview shows it at phone and desktop sizes. The button appears only after a successful submission. A connection failure leaves the response screen open so the visitor can retry rather than being sent to the contact destination.

Chart downloads now place long answer labels beneath the chart instead of cutting them off. The selected date range appears in the image footer. Anonymous responses contain no exportable email address because the visitor's address is removed before storage, including when the visitor comes through a campaign email. Owners can also choose whether unanswered questions appear as a separate category in the downloaded chart.

Administrators will see a new link-type column in the survey list. It records the mode of the most recently created share link and opens the full link history when selected. We fixed an error that occasionally showed a completed survey as still in progress after a browser refresh. For local installations, the release package checks the email-removal migration before enabling anonymous links; failed checks leave those links unavailable and display the record count needing attention. Back up the database before applying the package.

paragraphs.text: Survey room 7.2 adds anonymous links, a clearer completion screen, and additional chart labels. The update is available to all workspaces today and applies to surveys created before the release as well as new ones.

Anonymous links now discard the visitor's email address before a response is saved. The resulting response has no email field that an owner can export, even if the visitor arrived from an email campaign. Choose an anonymous link from the Share menu; existing identified campaign links remain identified. The link preview shows which mode you selected.

Completion screens can include a contact button. Survey owners choose its label and destination, and the preview shows it at phone and desktop sizes. The button appears only after a successful submission. A connection failure leaves the response screen open so the visitor can retry rather than being sent to the contact destination.

Chart downloads now place long answer labels beneath the chart instead of cutting them off. The selected date range appears in the image footer. Anonymous responses contain no exportable email address because the visitor's address is removed before storage, including when the visitor comes through a campaign email. Owners can also choose whether unanswered questions appear as a separate category in the downloaded chart.

Administrators will see a new link-type column in the survey list. It records the mode of the most recently created share link and opens the full link history when selected. # Reading room 4.0

The new release introduces collection-level permissions. A collection owner can grant access to an entire collection, while document owners can still share individual documents. Existing document links retain their permissions after the update.

## Collections

The collection page lists members and their roles. A reader can open documents and comments. An editor can also add documents and change collection descriptions. Owners can change membership and remove the collection. The role descriptions are visible when inviting someone, so an owner can choose without leaving the dialog.

Search results now include a collection filter. Results are limited to documents the person searching can open, including individually shared documents in collections they cannot browse. The filter therefore narrows accessible results rather than granting access to the rest of a collection. Saved searches keep their current keywords and can be updated with a collection choice.

## Documents

The sharing panel separates access inherited from a collection from access granted directly on a document. A person can have both. Removing the collection role leaves the direct grant in place, and the panel shows that remaining grant immediately. This is particularly relevant when a collaborator leaves a project but continues advising on one paper.

## Checking a departure

To remove all of a departing collaborator's access, open Members, select the collaborator, and choose Review access. The review lists collection roles and direct document grants together. Remove the entries that should end, then export the remaining-access list for the project owner. Reviewing both sources avoids assuming that removing a collection role also removed an individual share.

The release also improves keyboard focus in footnote dialogs and fixes printing of long reference lists. Local administrators should export their membership list before installation. The installer preserves existing grants and produces a conversion log for checking the new collection roles against that export.

# Workshop register 2.9

The attendance register now supports late arrivals. Staff can record the time a participant joins without changing the session's scheduled start. The attendance export carries both times, so organizers can distinguish an on-time session from an individual arriving after it began.

Session notes can be pinned. A pinned note stays above the chronological note list until unpinned, making access arrangements or equipment changes easier to find. Several notes can be pinned, and their order follows the time each was pinned. Regular notes retain their original timestamps when another note is moved above them.

The equipment request form now accepts quantities larger than ninety-nine. Requests with more items than the venue holds show a warning and can be saved as drafts while staff arrange a loan. Confirmed requests still require a named staff member. Late-arrival records preserve the planned session time and separately store when the participant joined, allowing the export to distinguish session timing from individual punctuality.

## Forms and exports

Printed registers include a wider signature column and a small box for recording a late-arrival time by hand. The print preview shows the venue phone number in the footer. Pinned notes remain at the head of the note list until staff unpin them, with multiple pinned notes arranged by their pinning times. Exported participant names now retain accented characters in spreadsheet applications.

## Updating

Browser users receive these changes overnight. Staff using the offline register should send any completed sessions before updating the tablet app. Unsent sessions remain on the tablet, but a successful send before installation provides a server copy to compare if anything looks wrong afterwards. We fixed a crash that could occur when rotating a tablet while a signature was being entered. Please include the tablet model and session number when reporting a new signature issue.

# Print queue 5.6

Print queue 5.6 adds held printing for shared devices. A held job waits in the queue until its owner releases it at the printer. It remains held after a workstation restart, and jobs held longer than one day are deleted automatically.

Workstation users can choose Hold at printer in the print dialog. The dialog displays the selected printer and paper size before the job is sent. A held job appears in My jobs with its page count, submission time, and deletion deadline. Cancelling it there removes it from the printer queue as well.

At the printer, staff can scan their badge and open My held jobs. Select the job, check the paper size, and choose Release. Logging out before release leaves the job held. This procedure is posted beside shared printers because staff may arrive without access to the original workstation. A job released on the wrong paper can be stopped with the printer's physical cancel button.

Administrators can choose a shorter deletion period for a printer in a public reception area. Reducing it from one day to two hours also changes the deadlines of jobs already held there. The confirmation screen lists how many waiting jobs will expire immediately. Jobs at other printers retain their existing deadlines.

Held printing changes when pages emerge, rather than who can access a file on a workstation. An unattended signed-in workstation can still expose the source document. Staff should lock the workstation before walking to the printer, and log out of the printer after collecting the pages. These actions protect different stages of the same task.

The update also corrects duplex defaults after a tray change and adds an administrator export of queue errors. Existing immediate-print settings remain selected until a user or administrator chooses held printing. Printer displays will restart once during the overnight deployment, while already completed jobs remain in the history.

# Resource desk 9.1

This month's release adds a borrowing extension request and a redesigned equipment calendar. The browser application updates automatically; loan-desk tablets receive the same functions after their next app update. Current loans keep their recorded due dates.

## Extensions

Borrowers can request an extension from the loan page. A request does not change the due date until a desk worker approves it. The borrower sees Pending beside the proposed date, and the existing due date remains visible. Desk staff receive a queue entry that includes later reservations for the same item.

Borrowers may add a note of up to five hundred characters. Notes appear in the extension queue and in the loan history after a decision. Staff can edit the proposed date before approving, and the confirmation message explains the date that was granted.

## Calendar

The equipment calendar can group items by storage location. An empty location remains visible if it has reservations later in the selected period. Printing the calendar includes a key for reserved, collected, and overdue items. The desk worker's chosen color scheme is retained in the PDF.

The current due date stays in force while an extension awaits approval; sending the request alone does not move it, and the proposed date is marked Pending. Calendar cells now open a side panel rather than navigating away, so staff can check several reservations without resetting the date range.

## Other changes

We fixed a screen-reader label on the borrower search and a rounding issue in damage-fee previews. Returned items can be filtered by inspection status, with the inspector's initials shown beside completed checks. Local administrators should finish active imports before installing. The release checks for unfinished import batches and reports their names before making any changes. Helpdesk staff can use that list to identify which desk needs to complete or cancel a batch.

Borrowers may add a note of up to five hundred characters. Notes appear in the extension queue and in the loan history after a decision. Staff can edit the proposed date before approving, and the confirmation message explains the date that was granted.

The equipment calendar can group items by storage location. An empty location remains visible if it has reservations later in the selected period. Printing the calendar includes a key for reserved, collected, and overdue items. The desk worker's chosen color scheme is retained in the PDF.

# Ticket office 3.0

Seats can now be held while a group organizer collects names. A hold reserves selected seats for a stated period, and the organizer can enter passenger details before paying. The default period is twenty-four hours. Venues can choose a shorter period for performances close to selling out.

The seating plan shows held seats with an outline rather than the solid mark used for sold seats. Staff can open a hold to see its organizer, expiry time, and contact number. Those details stay in the staff view; the public plan shows only that the seat is temporarily unavailable.

A held seat becomes available again when its hold expires. Expiry releases it back to sale. This happens automatically, including outside office hours. Organizers receive a reminder two hours beforehand, provided the hold lasts longer than two hours. A one-hour hold instead includes its deadline in the initial message.

The payment screen handles partial groups more clearly. If an organizer pays for six of eight held seats, those six become sold and the remaining two stay held until the original expiry time. Payment does not restart the hold clock. Staff can release the remaining seats immediately if the organizer confirms they are no longer needed.

For evening duty staff, the close-of-day list now distinguishes unpaid holds from paid bookings awaiting names. This prevents a booking from being cancelled merely because its passenger details are incomplete. Downloading the list includes the relevant payment or expiry time beside each entry.

Before leaving the desk, check holds expiring during the next shift, confirm contact numbers for groups still collecting names, and pass any paid bookings with missing details to the next staff member. The shift sheet groups these actions by their deadline. We also fixed a receipt issue affecting group names with apostrophes and improved the loading speed of large seating plans.

>

>
> - Put completed repairs on the collection bench.

> - Record attendance and cash on the handover sheet.

>

# Sound desk 1.8

Recording sessions can now be duplicated as templates. The duplicate keeps track names, input assignments, and effects settings, but starts without recorded audio. This provides a starting layout for a recurring session while keeping each day's recordings separate.

The file browser has a new Missing media view. It lists audio files that a session expects but cannot find at their recorded locations. Each row shows the original path and the track using the file. Relinking a row updates that session only; another session using the same file retains its own path until opened and relinked.

To prepare a weekly programme, open the previous session, choose Duplicate as template, and give the new session a dated name. Check that the expected inputs are still connected before recording. The new session has the old track layout without yesterday's audio, so starting a take will create files for the new programme. Save it in the current week's folder before bringing guests into the room.

To prepare an empty layout for a different computer, duplicate as a template and choose Collect settings when saving. Copy the resulting folder to the second computer, then select its available inputs when prompted. Hardware names may differ even when both rooms have two microphones.

Meter labels are easier to read at the smaller display scale, and the headphone test now announces the selected output by name. We corrected a problem that could hide a track when its height was reduced below the minimum.

The installer leaves existing sessions unchanged. Before moving any recording archive, close its sessions and copy the full media folder, then open one copied session to test playback. The new template feature is intended for fresh recordings; archive copies still need their recorded audio.

# Member desk: May update

The May release improves household records and event sign-in. It is available in the browser today, and the front-desk app will update when it next connects. Membership numbers remain unchanged.

## Household records

A household can now have two billing contacts. Both contacts receive renewal notices, but the household still gets one invoice. Adding another contact therefore gives both people the renewal information without creating a second charge. Existing households begin with their current billing contact and can add another under Household settings.

Contact preferences are now shown beside each person rather than on a separate tab. A postal preference includes the address it will use. Staff can correct that address from the same panel, and the change is recorded under the editor's name in the household history.

For renewals, two billing contacts mean both receive the notice while only one invoice is issued to the household. This lets both contacts see the renewal without duplicating the charge. Staff can also mark a contact as temporarily away, which adds a dated note to the front-desk view.

## Events

The sign-in screen accepts a booking reference as well as a membership number. Guest bookings show the name supplied by the organizer and the number of places reserved. Staff can record a party arriving in two groups without creating a second booking. A remaining-places count stays visible until everyone has arrived.

The event export includes arrival times and the initials of the staff member who checked each party in. It also shows cancellations recorded after the event began, making them easier to distinguish from early cancellations. Sending renewal notices to both billing contacts does not create another household invoice; both receive the information and the household is charged once.

We fixed the print alignment on small membership cards. Please print a test card after updating a front-desk workstation before using a full sheet of blanks.

documents.text:
I recommend Bracken Cycles if we retain all twenty bicycles. Its annual inspection price is higher than Rowan's, but the price includes collection and return. Rowan charges for each collection, which makes the cheaper inspection rate less useful for a fleet kept at two sites.

Bracken quoted 48 pounds per bicycle, or 960 pounds for the fleet. Rowan quoted 39 pounds, or 780 pounds, plus 65 pounds for each collection and return journey. With one service round from each site, Rowan's total would be 910 pounds. On that narrow comparison Rowan remains cheaper by 50 pounds. Both include brake adjustment, wheel checks, and a written condition sheet; replacement parts are charged separately.

The difference is how they handle bicycles that fail inspection. Bracken will return serviceable bicycles immediately and bring repaired bicycles back later within the same collection price. Rowan would charge another journey if repairs outlast the first service visit. Last year seven bicycles needed parts, and they returned on three dates as the parts arrived. Even one extra Rowan journey would remove its initial price advantage.

Rowan offers a Saturday drop-off option that could avoid those charges. It would require staff to move the bicycles between sites and transport them to the workshop. Our van can carry five at a time, and Saturday visitor bookings use the van for the morning equipment run. I have therefore excluded self-delivery from the operating comparison.

Choose Bracken for the twenty-bike fleet: its 50-pound premium over the first Rowan collection round covers the separate returns we are likely to need and avoids a transport task we cannot reliably staff. If the committee reduces the fleet to ten bicycles at one site, ask both suppliers for new prices before signing. The collection pattern, which drives this recommendation, would then be different.

Coffee machine quotes for the foyer

# Payroll bureau renewal

## Service coverage

I compared the renewal from West Ledger with the proposal from Harbour Pay. Both cover monthly payroll for our twenty-three employees, pension submissions, and year-end forms. West Ledger also includes corrections requested within three working days of a pay run; Harbour charges 30 pounds for each corrected run. Our managers often submit late overtime, so included corrections favor West Ledger. West Ledger is the better fit for the way our hours are finalized.

## Access and records

Harbour has a staff portal for downloading payslips. West Ledger supplies password-protected files to the office, which sends them to staff. The portal would remove that distribution task, although staff without regular email access would still need help. Harbour demonstrated the portal on a phone and provided an example of the leaver-access process.

Both bureaus retain the payroll records for the period stated in their agreements and provide a complete export when the service ends. West Ledger's export is included in the annual fee. Harbour includes one export at termination and charges for additional requests during the contract. We should schedule any midyear data request with our accountant rather than ordering separate files for each query.

## Calendar

The renewal would begin on 1 January. Harbour needs employee details by 10 December to perform a parallel calculation, while West Ledger can continue without a transfer. The office has a year-end stocktake in the same week, and we have identified a staff member who could prepare the transfer file if needed. Because late overtime frequently leads to corrections, West Ledger's included correction service suits our pay process better. West Ledger is the better fit for the way our hours are finalized.

## Approval

The finance manager has authority to renew within the existing budget. If approved this week, I will confirm the payroll calendar and ask West Ledger to send the coming year's named contact list. The renewal document and both sample exports are attached for the accountant's records.

The initial recommendation is Oakline's folding chair. It is the only quoted model that can be moved upstairs in stacks of six on our existing trolley. The Merton chair is more comfortable in a long sitting, so I tested whether that benefit justified changing our storage arrangements.

The training room holds thirty people. Oakline quoted 44 pounds per chair and Merton 59 pounds. Both prices include delivery to the ground-floor entrance. Oakline's seat is slightly narrower, but its frame folds flat. Merton's moulded seat stacks vertically and needs a taller trolley, which would not pass beneath the stair landing when loaded to the supplier's recommended height.

We tried six of each model during Tuesday's two-hour course. Participants rated Merton more comfortable, particularly during the final discussion. Two participants asked for a cushion on Oakline. The room coordinator can store six washable cushions in the teaching cupboard, and the cushion supplier quoted 72 pounds for that set. Adding cushions would bring Oakline's total to 1,392 pounds, compared with 1,770 pounds for Merton before buying a trolley.

A permanent Merton stack in the training room would avoid the landing problem. It would also occupy the space used for practical demonstrations, which take place twice a week. Moving that stack aside still requires staff to lift and rebuild it. Oakline chairs can leave the room entirely after a session. The caretaker confirmed there is ground-floor cupboard space for all thirty folded chairs.

Buy thirty Oakline chairs and six cushions. That choice keeps the demonstration area clear, uses the trolley and cupboard we already have, and addresses the comfort issue at a total below the Merton chair price alone. Before ordering, ask Oakline to confirm that the delivered chairs match the sample's folded thickness; the cupboard calculation depends on that measurement.
